denial.premise_measurement: ZERO builds spent. `python tools/gdl/fnasm.py game/game/controls.c EnablePlayerControls --diff` at 0f4151839 accounts for every instruction of the delta, and all of it is one web. The TARGET materialises the constant 0 ONCE into a callee-saved register and COPIES it six times: `@0x14 li r27,0`, then `@0x18 addi r26,r27,0` (i = 0), `@0x2c stw r27,0(0) @lbl_803445FC(EMB_SDA21)`, `@0x48 addi r3,r27,0` (j = 0), `@0x54 stwx r27,r4,r3`, `@0x58 stwx r27,r5,r3` and `@0x70 stw r27,2008(r3)`. It also hoists the inner-loop trip count out of the outer loop: `@0x28 li r31,12` feeding `@0x40 mtctr r31`. OURS rematerialises instead, inside the loop: `@0x34 li r0,12` feeding `@0x3c mtctr r0`, `@0x44 li r0,0` plus `@0x48 mr r3,r0` where the target writes the single `@0x48 addi r3,r27,0`, and `@0x6c li r0,0` before `@0x74 stw r0,2008(r3)`. Counted: the target emits 6 `li` and 11 `addi` and no `mr`; we emit 8 `li`, 9 `addi` and 1 `mr` -- exactly `target-only: +2 addi ours-only: -2 li -1 mr`, net +1, which is the whole 39-vs-40 gap. The consequence is visible in the prologue: the target's `@0x10 stmw r26,8(r1)` saves SIX callee-saved registers at frame 32 because 0 and 12 live in two of them, while our `@0x10 stmw r28,8(r1)` saves FOUR at frame 24. There is no structural difference anywhere else in either function. THE SCREEN: `gdlmem.py laws --query 'live zero copy remat'` returns claim.law.live-zero-copy-vs-remat-is-allocator-not-source.20260831.v1 as ESTABLISHED with 58 citations, n=30, 30 successes, ZERO failures, wilson 0.8865, and its head states the choice between `li rD,0` and `addi rD,rS,0` is made by MWCC's register allocator, is not reachable by any initializer spelling, is BIDIRECTIONAL across the corpus, and is 'the single most-retried dead residual in the corpus' across at least twelve functions in eight TUs -- naming, among the forms already killed, separate literal zeros, chained assignment, copy-from-the-other-variable, arithmetic initializers, combined for-init, signedness changes, block and nested scoping, declaration-initializer versus statement split, declaration reordering, register storage hints, staging locals and scoped `#pragma opt_propagation off`. The two run-50 records on this pair (attempt.SS_playercontrols-the-call-site-class-buys-only-a-compensating-pad-and-the-helper-sits-on-the-inline-threshold.20260903.v1 and attempt.SL_playercontrols-pair-inline-argument-substitution-is-not-pragma-reachable.20260903.v1) framed the residual as a CALL-SITE ARGUMENT class and spent three probe forms on it; SS's own premise_measurement records that after its best probe 'every remat the axis was aimed at survives verbatim: li r0,12 before mtctr, li r0,0 + mr r3,r0 for j = z, li r0,0 before stw r0,2008(r3)' -- which is this law's signature, written out, unrecognised. The call-site framing is therefore the wrong classification, and the family it belongs to already has a corpus-wide do-not-retry.

hypothesis.statement: Do not probe this pair again on the source axis. The one thing still worth doing costs zero builds and belongs to a naming lane, not a matching lane: the Xbox PDB gives this helper a real name. `context EnablePlayerControls` returns CONTROLS.OBJ neighbours in source order -- ClearAllPlayerControls (ordinal 48), InitPlayerControls (49), ResetPlayerControls (50), DisablePlayerControls (51), EnablePlayerControls (52) -- so our invented static `reset_player_controls` sits exactly where the PDB has `ResetPlayerControls`, with four of the five surrounding names already matching ours letter for letter. Run `gdlmem.py symaudit --tu game/game/controls` and, if it confirms the position, adopt it with `gdlmem.py rename-symbol reset_player_controls ResetPlayerControls --apply`. That is a spelling change to a static helper, so it cannot move any score; it is banked here because it is the only remaining actionable item on the pair and it would otherwise be lost with the park.
